newsitem.title: FRANCE: France, Germany vow no delay to EMU.
newsitem.headline: France, Germany vow no delay to EMU.

text.p: France and Germany, leaders in the drive to monetary union, vowed on Wednesday that there would be no delay to plans to launch a single European currency in January 1999.

"The timetable for Economic and Monetary Union will be respected. I have no doubt about that," French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis told a news conference after a meeting with German Finance Minister Theo Waigel and the central bank heads of the two countries.
Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said the question of delaying the single currency had "most definitely not" played a part in the talks in the central French city of Lyon.
The meeting, one of a regular series between Europe's two biggest economies, took place amid speculation EMU might be delayed to give Bonn time to meet Maastricht treaty criteria.
Economists say they doubted Germany, meant to be Europe's model economy, could cut its budget deficit to three percent of gross domestic product this year as required by Maastricht.
Arthuis said he was confident France and Germany would be ready for EMU, helped by growth in both countries of nearly 2.5 percent this year after a temporary slowdown last year.

"We now have a chance to use our growth-oriented policies to achieve our goal," Waigel said. Talk of alternatives to the euro, as the single currency is to be known, is "not productive and not necessary," he said.
